h1: Traffic Warrant Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: A missed ticket date in El Paso County turns into a warrant, a second charge and a block on your license renewal. Attorney Robert Navar can usually have the warrant recalled in a day or two — without you going to jail or to court.
summary: A traffic warrant in El Paso is almost always a Class C matter. It can be recalled by the court when an attorney files an appearance and posts a bond — you do not have to be arrested to clear it.
Missing a court date is a separate offense (Transportation Code 543.009), so most people with one warrant actually have two cases: the original ticket and the failure to appear.
An OMNI hold under Transportation Code Chapter 706 blocks your Texas license renewal until the court clears it; see OMNI hold removal.
Our fee is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional, on top of the flat ticket fee. Start with the free warrant lookup.

sections.heading: How a Traffic Ticket Becomes a Warrant in El Paso County
paragraphs: Every El Paso citation carries an appearance date, usually 10 to 20 days out. If nothing happens by that date — no payment, no plea, no attorney on file — the court mails a notice and then issues a warrant. In El Paso Municipal Court that process can run in a matter of weeks; the Justice of the Peace precincts and the smaller city courts move at their own pace, but they all get there. The result is a bench warrant on the original ticket plus a new citation for failing to appear, each with its own fine and court costs.

Most people find out one of three ways: a letter from the court, a traffic stop where the officer runs the plate, or a trip to the DPS office where the clerk says the license cannot be renewed. That last one is the OMNI hold — the Failure to Appear program the courts report into, which denies renewal until the clerk sends DPS a clearance. We wrote about how the whole chain works in El Paso warrants lifted. None of it is unusual; the point is to handle it on your schedule, not during a stop on Loop 375 at midnight.

sections.heading: How Warrant Recall Works — Usually Without Jail or Court
paragraphs: When you hire us, we file a notice of appearance and an attorney bond or motion to recall with the court that issued the warrant. For a Class C traffic warrant, that filing is usually enough: the judge signs the recall, the clerk pulls the warrant from the active list, and the case is reset to a pretrial docket where we negotiate it like any other ticket. In El Paso Municipal Court this commonly takes 24 to 48 hours; the JP and smaller city courts take a few days. Our traffic warrant recall page walks through the steps court by court.

You do not turn yourself in, you do not wait in the jail lobby for a magistrate, and in most cases you do not appear at all. Once the warrant is recalled, the original ticket and the failure-to-appear charge are both still open — and that is where the defense work starts. The failure-to-appear case is often dismissed as part of resolving the underlying ticket; we explain the leverage on the failure to appear defense page. If the hold has already blocked your license, we ask the court to send DPS the OMNI clearance as soon as the case is set — see OMNI hold removal. Our older warrant lawyer page is still online for clients who found us there.

sections.heading: What a Warrant Costs to Clear
paragraphs: Our warrant fee is simple: $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one, added to the flat ticket fee of $59 in Municipal Court or $69 in JP and the smaller city courts. A single old speeding ticket with a warrant in El Paso Municipal Court is therefore $94 with the warrant gone; add-on citations are discounted and each extra warrant is $20.

Court costs are separate and depend on the outcome; the court usually assesses its own warrant fee, and the OMNI clearance carries a small administrative fee DPS collects at renewal. We do not charge separately for the OMNI letter when we are already resolving the case. You can hire online and see the total at checkout before you pay.

faqs.q: Will I be arrested for a traffic warrant in El Paso?
faqs.a: You can be, usually during a traffic stop, which is the reason to act first. For Class C traffic warrants an attorney can file a recall and bond so the warrant is pulled from the active list without you being booked.

faqs.q: How long does it take to lift a traffic warrant?
faqs.a: In El Paso Municipal Court, typically 24 to 48 hours after we file. Justice of the Peace precincts and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts usually take a few business days. We tell you as soon as the clerk confirms the recall.

faqs.q: Why does the warrant show two cases when I only got one ticket?
faqs.a: Missing the appearance date is its own Class C offense under Transportation Code 543.009, so the court files a failure-to-appear case alongside the original ticket. Both have to be resolved. The failure-to-appear charge is frequently dismissed as part of settling the first ticket.

faqs.q: I paid the ticket but DPS still won't renew my license. Why?
faqs.a: The court has to send DPS an OMNI clearance after the case closes, and that step sometimes lags or gets missed. We can contact the clerk, confirm the case is closed, and get the clearance sent so the hold drops. See OMNI hold removal.
